messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Traffic Laws & Regulations – State of Texas** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary from 35‑55 mph on rural roads to 70–75 mph on interstates.
• “No Speed Limit” zones exist only on some county highways where posted signs read *“NO SPEED LIMIT.”*
• Exceeding the limit by more than 20 % may trigger a ticket even without a sign. | | **Seat Belt / Child Restraint** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years old who weigh < 80 lb must ride in a rear‑facing child safety seat until age 2 or weight ≥ 40 lb.
• After age 2, children up to 5 years old must remain in a forward‑ward facing car seat unless no other option exists. | | **Texting/Phone Use** | • Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited except when using hands‑free devices.
• Texting while operating a vehicle is illegal regardless of whether you’re stopped at a red light. | | **DUI/DWI** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) > 0.08 % constitutes DWI for adults; lower thresholds apply to commercial drivers (< 0.04 %) and minors (< 0.01 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching first have priority.
• Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks marked with zebra stripes or flashing lights.
• School buses stopping to pick up/drop off students require all lanes to stop behind the bus’s stop line. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay within their lane unless turning left/right or passing another vehicle.
• Passing on the right is allowed only when the preceding driver is making a left turn or traveling slower than the speed limit. | | **Parking Restrictions** | • No parking within 15 ft of a fire hydrant, intersection curb, or pedestrian crossing.
• Parking on sidewalks is generally prohibited unless otherwise signed. | | **Vehicle Equipment Requirements** | • Headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, horn, windshield wipers, and mirrors must be functional.
• Tires must meet minimum tread depth requirements (1/16″ for passenger cars, 3⁄32″ for trucks). | | **Driving Under Influence of Drugs** | • Prescription drugs that impair driving ability can lead to DUI charges if impairment is proven.
• Certain recreational substances (e.g., marijuana) are still considered disqualifying if they affect safe operation. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Tex. Veh. Code §545.001 et seq.** | Official statutory text covering most traffic rules. | | **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** | Driver handbook, licensing info, penalty schedules. | | **Texas Highway Patrol website** | Enforcement priorities, recent updates, public service announcements. | | **Legal Aid websites** | Summaries of common violations and court procedures. | --- #### Quick Reference Links - [TX DMV Traffic Law Handbook](https://www.txdmv.gov/) - [Texas Vehicle Code Online](http://statelaws.findlaw.com/state-laws/Texas.html) - [Highways Patrol – Safety Tips](https://www.dps.texas.gov/highways-patrol) Feel free to let me know if you need details on a particular rule—such as school‑bus protocols, toll‑road usage, or how penalties differ between counties—and I’ll dig deeper!
